issues.display_title: Issue #1556: [Foundation][Integration] ThemeService + dark/light theme toggle
issues.main_description_html:
Epic: Foundation (integration)

Implement dark/light theme switching driven by a ThemeService.

Scope

  • ThemeService sets data-theme on <html>, persists choice (storage), SSR-safe default.
  • Theme toggle UI in the shared header (always visible).
  • Theme colors the shared shell (everywhere) + marketing bodies. Product page bodies stay light.

Acceptance criteria

  • Toggling switches theme instantly; choice persists across reloads and navigation.
  • No window/document access at module load (SSR-safe); correct default rendered on server.

Testing scenario (QA)

  1. Click the theme toggle → header/footer + marketing page switch to dark; reload → still dark (persisted).
  2. Navigate to a product page (editor/settings) → header/footer dark, page body stays light.
  3. Hard-refresh in dark mode → no flash of light theme before hydration.
  4. Open in a fresh/incognito session → loads with the correct default theme.

Demo by Developer

issues.display_title: Issue #1554: [Foundation] Scoped design tokens & theme variables (SCSS)
issues.main_description_html:
Epic: Foundation (design system)

Introduce the new design-system styling as additive global SCSS, scoped so it does not affect product pages.

Scope

  • Define design tokens as CSS custom properties.
  • :root / [data-theme] → shell tokens (header/footer/theme colors) — apply app-wide.
  • .vm-marketing wrapper class → marketing body tokens (Geist typography, spacing, hero/card/grid styles) — marketing pages only.
  • Provide light + dark value sets for both scopes.

Acceptance criteria

  • Tokens available globally; marketing tokens only take effect inside .vm-marketing.
  • No visual change to editor/settings/profile/billing pages.

Testing scenario (QA)

  1. Open any product page (editor, settings) before/after the change — confirm no visual difference (pixel/visual diff).
  2. Add a temporary element with .vm-marketing and confirm new typography/spacing tokens apply only inside it.
  3. Toggle data-theme="dark" on <html> and confirm shell token colors change while product page bodies stay unchanged.

issues.display_title: Issue #1555: [Foundation] Self-host Geist / Geist Mono fonts
issues.main_description_html:
Epic: Foundation (design system)

Self-host the Geist and Geist Mono fonts used by the new design.

Scope

  • Add self-hosted Geist / Geist Mono web fonts (woff2) with font-display: swap.
  • Wire into the marketing typography tokens.
  • Google Fonts only as fallback.

Acceptance criteria

  • Fonts load on marketing pages without layout shift (CLS) issues.
  • SSR build serves fonts correctly (no FOUT/blocking).

Testing scenario (QA)

  1. Load /about on a throttled (Slow 3G) connection — text renders with fallback then swaps to Geist; no blank text.
  2. Verify in DevTools > Network that fonts are served from our domain (self-hosted), not blocked.
  3. Check CLS in Lighthouse is within budget on marketing pages.

issues.display_title: Issue #1557: [Foundation][Integration] revealOnScroll directive (SSR-safe)
issues.main_description_html:
Epic: Foundation (integration)

Reimplement the static site's scroll-reveal animation as an Angular directive.

Scope

  • revealOnScroll directive using IntersectionObserver.
  • SSR no-op (guard with isPlatformBrowser); elements visible by default if JS/observer unavailable.
  • Replaces the .reveal behavior from assets/app.js.

Acceptance criteria

  • Elements animate in on scroll in the browser.
  • Server-rendered HTML shows content (no hidden content if JS disabled).

Testing scenario (QA)

  1. Scroll down a marketing page → sections fade/slide in as they enter the viewport.
  2. Disable JavaScript → all content is still visible (not stuck hidden).
  3. View page source (SSR) → content present in HTML.

Demo by Developer

Testing scenario (QA)

  2. curl / view-source each marketing route — meaningful HTML returned (not just an empty app shell).
  3. Load each route in the browser — hydrates without console errors.

  • Real reCAPTCHA (replace mock checkbox).
  • Real file upload: Help Center screenshot (JPG/JPEG/PNG ≤10MB); Custom multi-file (JPG/PNG/DOC/DOCX/PDF) with type/size validation.
  • Validation, success and error states (via real flow + alert-message).

Acceptance criteria

  • Each form validates, passes reCAPTCHA, uploads files, submits to backend, and shows real success/error.

Testing scenario (QA)

  1. Submit General Inquiries with valid data → backend receives it; success state shows.
  2. Submit with empty required fields → inline validation blocks submit.
  3. Fail/skip reCAPTCHA → submit blocked with message.
  4. Help Center: upload an oversized (>10MB) or wrong-type file → rejected with message; valid PNG → accepted and submitted.
  5. Custom request: upload multiple mixed valid files (PDF/DOCX/PNG) → accepted; submit → backend receives files + fields.
  6. Simulate backend error → error state shown; user can retry.
